title: What Are the Best AI Inference Providers in 2026?
summary: Compare fal, Together AI, Fireworks AI, AWS, Google Cloud and Azure on AI model coverage, pricing, speed, reliability and deployment control.
body_markdown:
You need an inference provider for a product, but the best starting point depends on what the application generates. Media models, text workloads, custom deployment and GPU infrastructure place different demands on the service you choose. A broad provider ranking can hide those differences behind the same API label.


This guide separates generative-media routes from text-oriented options before comparing deployment and scaling workflows. You’ll see where catalog access helps and where running your own model changes the decision. Start with the required input, output and operation, then evaluate the provider around that production job rather than its feature count.


## Quick answer


**Choose an inference provider around the output and deployment route your product needs.**


This comparison treats generative-media catalogs, text inference and custom model hosting as different decisions. Confirm the exact endpoint and operational requirements before selecting a platform.


## TL;DR


- **Best for generative media: fal.** fal leads the market with high-speed runtimes, large model catalogs, and flexible serverless inference or dedicated GPU options.
- **Day-0 access to new models: fal.** fal is a day-0 partner for the most popular AI models like Seedance 2.5, MiniMax H3 and more.
- **Best for open-weight text: Together AI or Fireworks AI.** Both price per token. Fireworks dropped image generation in June 2026, and Together passes most image requests through to outside providers.
- **Best inside one cloud: AWS, Google Cloud or Azure.** Their media catalogs are narrow, and default media quotas are small.
- **What to compare:** cost per accepted output, queue behavior during bursts, and the published SLA, not just the list price.

## How we evaluated the providers


fal serves every API-available model in the current top five of Artificial Analysis's text-to-image, text-to-video and image-to-video leaderboards. It puts[1,400+ model endpoints](https://fal.ai/inference) behind one API. Its own post-trained video model, MiniMax H3 Max, ranks #1 on Design Arena's image-to-video board. And the same serverless runtime that serves fal's catalog can power your own models too with a developer friendly deployment setup.


For image, video and audio products, compare providers on the criteria in this checklist. Tokens per second alone does not describe the time or cost of delivering a usable media file.


1. **Model coverage:** whether the models your users actually want are available, especially the ones at the top of independent leaderboards.
2. **Time to new models:** whether a new release is callable on launch day or weeks later.
3. **Speed:** independent measurements where they exist, and vendor claims labeled as such.
4. **Cost:** the billing unit, what's billed when something fails or sits idle, and cost per accepted output.
5. **Behavior under bursts:** rate limits, concurrency limits and whether excess requests are queued or rejected.
6. **Custom models:** whether you can run your own weights, pipelines and containers on the same platform.
7. **Reliability:** the published SLA, and what it covers.
8. **Enterprise readiness:** security certifications, access controls, data retention and regions.
9. **Enterprise adoption:** documented customers and production use cases relevant to your workload.


The stakes are rising too. Gartner expects global spending on inference to pass spending on training for the first time in 2026, at $23.3 billion against $19 billion,[according to CIO Dive](https://www.ciodive.com/news/AI-spending-soars-enterprise-maturity/827488/) .


## 1. fal: the best inference provider for generative media


fal is an inference platform built for generative media. It runs three products on one runtime:


- **Model APIs:** hosted models behind one key and one client, billed per output.
- **Serverless:** your own models on the same runtime, billed per second.
- **Compute:** dedicated GPUs with SSH, for training and long jobs.


### Model coverage


fal has the most complete coverage of top-ranked generative media models of any provider in this comparison.


- **1,400+ model endpoints** behind one API, according to[fal.ai/inference](https://fal.ai/inference) . fal's public model API listed 1,506 active endpoints on October 14, 2026: 607 image, 550 video, 160 audio and 67 3D, plus 59 training and 63 other endpoints.
- **Every API-available top-five model.** fal is the only provider here with all 10 of the top-five models from Artificial Analysis's three media leaderboards.
- **Labs on one bill.** Models from Google, OpenAI, Black Forest Labs, ByteDance, MiniMax, xAI, Alibaba, Kling, ElevenLabs, Luma, Lightricks (LTX), Ideogram, Bria and others sit behind the same API.
- **More than generation.** fal also hosts editing, upscaling, lip sync, avatars, speech-to-text, music, sound effects, image-to-3D and LoRA training endpoints.


### Time to new models


fal routinely ships new media models on launch day. It was a[day-0 ecosystem partner for MiniMax H3](https://fal.ai/minimax-h3) , and[Kling 3.0 was available on fal from day zero](https://blog.fal.ai/kling-3-0-is-now-available-on-fal/) . Per[fal.ai/inference](https://fal.ai/inference) , new models from leading labs go live with an API endpoint and a playground on day one.


fal also trains and serves its own models.[MiniMax H3 Max](https://fal.ai/minimax-h3-max) is fal Research's post-trained version of the open-weight MiniMax H3,[trained on fal Compute and served on fal Serverless](https://blog.fal.ai/h3-max-built-with-fal-inference-and-training/) . fal and MiniMax released it jointly; besides fal, it's available through MiniMax's own API and Runware.


### Speed


Speed is a core focus for fal. fal says its[Inference Engine](https://fal.ai/inference) is up to 10x faster, using custom CUDA kernels, optimized attention layers and inference-engine tuning. Independent and published evidence:


- **Design Arena, image-to-video.** H3 Max ranks #1 with an Elo of 1,328, tied with Pruna's P-Video-2-Pro. Its average generation time is 5.6 seconds, against 239.5 seconds for base MiniMax H3, 237.2 seconds for Seedance 2.5 and 157.7 seconds for Wan 3.0 ([leaderboard](https://www.designarena.ai/leaderboard/image-to-video) , October 14, 2026).
- **Artificial Analysis, MiniMax H3 providers.** fal returned a 5-second clip in a median of about 10 seconds, second-fastest of seven providers. MiniMax's own API took about two minutes. fal was also second-cheapest, at $3.60 per minute against MiniMax's $4.80 ([provider page](https://artificialanalysis.ai/video/providers/minimax-h3-768p) , trailing three-day median on October 14, 2026).
- **Ideogram v4.** fal cut 1K image generation from 2.75 seconds to 0.44 seconds using NVFP4, kernel fusion and distillation,[without quality loss](https://blog.fal.ai/serving-sub-second-ideogram-v4-without-quality-loss/) .
- **H3 Max on fal's benchmark.** H3 Max returns a 5-second 768p video in under 3 seconds end to end ([fal.ai/minimax-h3-max](https://fal.ai/minimax-h3-max) ).


Artificial Analysis also places H3 Max in the top tier of its video leaderboards: fifth on text-to-video and image-to-video with audio, inside a statistically tied range of second to sixth. Rankings move often, so check the live boards before you commit to any model.


### Cost


Most Model APIs bill per output, so you pay for images, megapixels, video seconds or characters rather than GPU time. A few less common models without a fixed output price bill per second of GPU time instead. You're never billed for time in the queue or for requests that fail with a server error ([pricing docs](https://fal.ai/docs/documentation/model-apis/pricing) ). For your own models,[Serverless](https://fal.ai/pricing) bills per second while runners are alive. An H100 is $4.50 per hour at list price and as low as $2.49, an RTX PRO 6000 is $4.00 and as low as $1.99, and B200, B300 and GB200 are available too. Waiting for a GPU and pulling your container image aren't billed.[Compute](https://fal.ai/docs/documentation/compute) instances bill per hour at rates quoted by the fal team.


### Deployment and control


- **Model APIs** support queued requests with webhooks, synchronous calls, streaming, and real-time WebSocket connections.
- [Serverless](https://fal.ai/serverless) runs your own Python app (` fal deploy` ), a custom container, an existing Docker or HTTP server, or a[ComfyUI workflow](https://fal.ai/docs/examples/image-generation/deploy-comfyui-server) . It's the same runtime that serves fal's own catalog, and it scales from zero to thousands of GPUs. Deployments are private by default and can be pinned to US or EU regions.
- [Compute](https://fal.ai/docs/documentation/compute) gives you dedicated H100 machines with full SSH access for training and fine-tuning.
- **Official clients** cover Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, Swift, Java, Kotlin and Dart. There are migration guides for Modal, RunPod and Baseten.


### Reliability under load


- **A 99.99% uptime SLA** is stated on the[fal Serverless page](https://fal.ai/serverless) , with[SLA guarantees](https://fal.ai/enterprise) on enterprise plans. fal's[status page](https://status.fal.ai/) reported 90-day uptime of 100.0% for the Serverless API and 99.97% for the Model API on October 14, 2026.
- **A queue that never drops work.** Requests are[never rejected because of concurrency limits](https://fal.ai/docs/documentation/model-apis/concurrency-limits) , and the queue has no size limit. Only running requests count against your limit.
- **Retries and fallbacks by default.** Queued requests that hit a transient failure (a 503, a 504, a connection error or a 429 rate limit) are retried automatically, up to 10 times, and supported models can fall back to an equivalent endpoint ([reliability docs](https://fal.ai/docs/documentation/model-apis/inference/reliability) ).
- **Faster cold starts.**[FlashPack](https://fal.ai/docs/documentation/serverless/optimizations/flashpack) streams weights straight to the GPU, and a three-layer cache keeps them close to your runners.


### Enterprise readiness and adoption


fal holds[SOC 2 Type II](https://trust.fal.ai/) , with SSO/SAML, model access controls, private endpoints and region pinning. fal[never trains its models on enterprise customers' data](https://fal.ai/enterprise) .


Teams listed on[fal.ai/inference](https://fal.ai/inference) include Adobe, Shopify, Canva, Quora, Perplexity, Genspark, Suno, World Labs, Lightricks, Bria, Moonvalley, HeyGen, VEED, Creatify and Doji. Suno's CTO credits fal Serverless with helping to make the Suno v6 rollout possible.


### What to plan for


- **Serverless cold starts.** New runners take time to start. Keep a warm floor with` min_concurrency` or reserve capacity for latency-critical traffic.
- **Concurrency on new accounts.** Model API accounts start at 2 concurrent requests, and the limit rises automatically as you buy credits, up to 40. Higher limits come through sales, and queued requests wait rather than fail.
- **Discounted GPU rates.** The as-low-as Serverless rates depend on volume and commitments, so ask the fal team for a quote.


**Best for:** any product that generates images, video, audio, 3D or world models, from a first prototype to production at scale, plus custom media models that need managed GPUs.


## 2. Together AI: open-weight LLMs and GPU clusters


Together AI is an open-model platform focused on language models, fine-tuning and GPU clusters. Its chief scientist is Tri Dao, who created FlashAttention.


### Model coverage


Together's[model library](https://www.together.ai/models) listed about 175 models on October 14, 2026, mostly chat, code and vision. It also offers image, video and audio models, but[Together's docs](https://docs.together.ai/docs/serverless/overview) say most image models are hosted by an external provider. Together passes the request through, and per-image prices are estimates rather than fixed rates. Video runs as an asynchronous job. Together's docs say video bills per second of output, while its pricing page lists one per-video price at the lowest resolution and duration and notes that actual prices might vary. Together has no 3D models, and carries 3 of the 10 top-ranked media models.


### Cost


Serverless text is priced per token. For example, gpt-oss-120B is $0.15 per million input tokens and $0.60 per million output tokens, and Kimi K3 is $3.00 and $15.00 ([pricing](https://www.together.ai/pricing) ). Other options:


- **Dedicated Model Inference** bills per GPU-minute while a replica is ready: $5.49 per hour for an H100 and $8.99 for a B200.
- **GPU clusters** cost $3.99 per H100-hour on demand, $1.99 preemptible, and $3.19 to $3.69 reserved for 3 to 180 days.
- **Batch** advertises up to 50% off, but the docs currently list only one model, Whisper Large v3, as discounted.


### Limits


- **No documented serverless SLA.** Together's docs call serverless[best-effort](https://docs.together.ai/docs/serverless/rate-limits) , with dynamic rate limits that can return 429 or 503 errors under high demand. Some Together model pages advertise a 99.9% SLA on serverless, but the docs define SLA terms only for Provisioned Throughput.
- **Provisioned Throughput** carries a[99% monthly SLA](https://docs.together.ai/docs/inference/provisioned-throughput) , but requires a one-month minimum and goes through sales. Together's[reliability post](https://www.together.ai/blog/99-9-uptime-for-inference) also lists a 99.9% contractual SLA for multi-data-center deployments.
- **Fine-tuned adapters** are served only on dedicated endpoints; serverless LoRA has been discontinued.
- **Fixed serverless region.** You can't choose where serverless runs.


**Best for:** open-weight LLM serving, fine-tuning, and renting GPU clusters for training. **Choose fal instead** for media generation: it carries all 10 top-ranked media models against Together's 3, and its queue holds requests during a spike, where Together's serverless tier can return 429 or 503 errors.


## 3. Fireworks AI: low-latency open-weight text and agents


Fireworks AI is an inference and training platform for open text and vision models, with a current focus on coding and agent workloads.


### Model coverage


Fireworks[deprecated image generation and audio inference on June 10, 2026](https://docs.fireworks.ai/updates/changelog) . It now offers no image, video or audio generation, and carries none of the 10 top-ranked media models.


Its library lists about 319 models, but only 14 are available on serverless: 13 per-token models plus FireRouter, a router for coding workloads. The rest need a dedicated deployment. Serverless is compatible with both the OpenAI and Anthropic APIs.


### Cost


Serverless is priced per token ([pricing docs](https://docs.fireworks.ai/serverless/pricing) ). For example, gpt-oss-120B is $0.15 input and $0.60 output per million tokens, Kimi K3 is $3.00 and $15.00, and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash is $0.30 and $1.20. Pricing varies by tier and region:


- **Batch** costs 50% less.
- **Priority** typically costs about 25% more, on supported models.
- **Fast** variants cost 1.5x, for Kimi K3 and GLM 5.3.
- **US-only** serverless models cost 1.5x since September 1, 2026.
- **Dedicated GPUs** bill per GPU-second: $8.00 per hour for an H100 or H200, $13.00 for a B200 and $15.00 for a B300. Region-restricted deployments cost 1.5x.


### Limits


- **No serverless SLA.** Serverless has[no SLA for latency or availability](https://docs.fireworks.ai/faq-new/deployment-infrastructure/is-latency-guaranteed-for-serverless-models) . A throughput SLA applies only to traffic within a Reserved Throughput purchase.
- **Rate limits.** An account-wide[cap of 6,000 requests per minute](https://docs.fireworks.ai/guides/quotas_usage/account-quotas) applies, and requests can still be load-shed with a 503.
- **Model churn.** Serverless models change frequently, with at least two weeks' notice before removal.


**Best for:** latency-sensitive text and agent workloads on open models, with a half-price Batch API for asynchronous jobs, a Priority tier that's less likely to be load-shed at peak, and Fast variants on select models. **Choose fal instead** for anything that generates media.


## 4. AWS, Google Cloud and Microsoft Azure: inference inside your cloud


The hyperscalers make sense when identity, procurement, data residency and governance already live in one cloud. All three are built mainly for text models, and their media catalogs are narrow.


### Amazon Web Services


- **Catalog:**[Amazon Bedrock](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-cards.html) lists 19 model providers.
- **Media models:** Stability AI image models ($0.04 to $0.14 per image), Luma Ray2 video ($0.75 to $1.50 per second, US West only) and Nova 2 Sonic speech ([pricing](https://aws.amazon.com/bedrock/pricing/) ). Amazon's own Nova Canvas and Nova Reel reached[end of life on September 30, 2026](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-lifecycle-legacy.html) .
- **Media quotas:** defaults are small. Luma Ray2 allows 1 concurrent request per region, and Stable Image Ultra allows 10 requests per minute ([quotas](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/bedrock.html) ).
- **Discounts and reserved capacity:** batch is 50% off, but only for select models that return text or embeddings; no image, video or speech generation model is eligible. Provisioned Throughput is available with no commitment, or on 1-month or 6-month terms.
- **SLA:**[99.9% monthly uptime](https://aws.amazon.com/bedrock/sla/) for Bedrock. Custom models run on SageMaker AI.


### Google Cloud


- **Platform:** Vertex AI became part of[Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/release-notes) on April 22, 2026. Model Garden lists 200+ models.
- **Media models:** Google-built only, including the Gemini "Nano Banana" image family (about $0.067 per 1K image for Nano Banana 2), Gemini Omni Flash video in preview, and Lyria music ([pricing](https://cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/generative-ai/pricing) ).
- **Discounts and reserved capacity:** Flex and Batch are 50% off Standard. Batch caps image output at 1K and is excluded from the SLA. Provisioned Throughput terms run from one week to one year and can't be canceled.
- **SLA:**[99.5% monthly uptime](https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/sla) for online inference.


### Microsoft Azure


- **Platform:** Azure AI Foundry is now[Microsoft Foundry](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/what-is-foundry) , with a catalog of over 10,000 models.
- **Media models sold directly by Azure:** OpenAI's GPT Image family, Black Forest Labs FLUX (FLUX 1.1 Pro is $0.04 per image) and Microsoft's MAI-Image in preview, plus OpenAI speech models. Its only video model, Sora 2 (preview), has an October 15, 2026 retirement date on Microsoft's schedule ([models](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/foundry-models/concepts/models-sold-directly-by-azure) ,[retirements](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/concepts/model-lifecycle-retirement) ,[pricing](https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/pricing/details/ai-foundry-models/black-forest-labs/) ).
- **Media quotas:** defaults are single-digit requests per minute for GPT Image 2 ([quotas](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/openai/quotas-limits) ).
- **Discounts:** the Batch API is 50% off, but covers language models only.
- **SLA:**[99.9% availability](https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/products/ai-foundry/models/openai) for Azure OpenAI.


**Best for:** enterprises consolidating AI spend on an existing cloud contract, mostly for text. **Choose fal instead** for media. Coverage is the gap: AWS carries none of the 10 top-ranked media models, Google 2 and Azure 3, against fal's 10. fal also announced a[strategic partnership with AWS](https://blog.fal.ai/fal-and-aws-building-for-the-next-phase-of-generative-media/) in May 2026.

## How to run a provider bake-off


### Step 1: Pin exactly what you're testing


Fix the model version, endpoint, resolution, duration, steps and any LoRAs, so every provider gets the same request.


### Step 2: Replay your real traffic


Test at the concurrency you expect at launch, including bursts. Separate cold and warm runs, and record queue time apart from generation time.


### Step 3: Measure what the user waits for


For media, measure time to a usable output, including the download, not just GPU time. Track P50 and P95.


### Step 4: Calculate cost per accepted output


**Cost per accepted output = total spend ÷ outputs that pass your quality bar**


Include retries, rejected generations and idle capacity. For example, at the $0.08-per-second list price, 1,000 ten-second MiniMax H3 Max clips at 768p cost $800 on fal. If 800 pass review, you paid $1.00 per accepted clip, not $0.80.


### Step 5: Read the terms that apply under load


Check the SLA and what it covers, rate limits, retention, region options, and whether failed requests are billed. Record the date you checked each one, because prices and leaderboards can change within weeks.

### When should I move from serverless to dedicated GPUs?


When the dedicated machine would be busy enough. The break-even utilization is the dedicated hourly price divided by the effective serverless hourly price. Below that, serverless is cheaper because you don't pay for idle time. There's no universal percentage, so calculate it with your own rates.


### How do I calculate cost per successful AI task?


Divide your total spend by the number of tasks that met your quality bar, including the cost of retries and rejected outputs. For token pricing, multiply input and output tokens by their per-million rates. For media, multiply the per-output price by the outputs you were billed for.


### How can I reduce cold starts on fal?


Set` keep_alive` to keep idle runners warm between requests, and` min_concurrency` to hold a warm floor. Use` concurrency_buffer` to absorb bursts, or reserved capacity for a guaranteed pool. Storing weights on` /data` and loading them with FlashPack also shortens each cold start.
